contexts.text: Some (perceive delight) in mud.
To tread the clay () = falsities.
They had bitumen for clay () = the evil of cupidity for good.
That clay = the good of which the mind or the man of the Church is formed, is evident from the Word. Illustrated.
Clay () = the man of the Church himself, who is being formed, thus it = the good of charity, through which is all formation of man, that is, reformation and regeneration.
Under Clay, see these references. AC 10030:4. AE 176:2. AE 237:end. AE 411:4.
In clay and in bricks () = on account of the evils which they found out and the falsities which they fashioned. Clay = good, and in the opposite sense, evil.
That clay = the evil from which is falsity, is evident from these passages in the Word. Illustrated.
Clay () = the man of the Church who is being formed, thus it = the good of faith, through which man is formed, that is, reformed.
To tread the clay = evil.
Houses woven of rushes stuck together with mud.
Like clay in the hand of the potter.
In mud over the ankles.
To enter into the mire and tread the clay = to confirm falsities by figments and fallacies.
The clay which He made in the soil with spittle () = reformation through truths from the sense of the letter of the Word... Clay = the ultimate Divine which forms. AE 304:61.
The waters which cast up mire and dirt () = falsities themselves from which are evils of life and falsities of doctrine.
As Divine truths in their ultimate are there, it is added, clay of great waters (); clay = the ultimate from which and in which.
Clay from spittle = sensuous truth, such as there is for such in the Word.
Snatch me out of the mire lest I sink () = out of the evil of falsity lest I perish.
As street = falsity, the mire of the streets () = the falsity of the love of evil.
